about: Founded on one simple belief: you deserve to understand what's happening in your body.

Menopause Understood exists for the woman moving through perimenopause, menopause or postmenopause who feels overwhelmed, unheard and unsure what's happening to her body. We meet her with warmth, clarity and genuine community, so she never has to work it out alone.
Hi, I'm Melissa Tahu. Welcome to Menopause Understood.

My journey here began with a simple shower. About three years into early menopause, I had more symptoms than I could count. I wasn't sleeping, I had chronic migraines, and I was hot, achy and irritable more days than not. I was juggling an undergraduate degree in Nutrition Science, kids, and family life, and I felt isolated, confused and sad. One morning during my shower, after another bad night's sleep, I looked down at a body that had changed overnight and thought, "Why did no one ever tell me about menopause? Surely I wasn't the only one going through this?"

Those questions led me to enrol in a Master of Medical Science, where I'm researching women's interactions with menopause health information and services. But the more research and women's stories that I read, the more it felt like I was reliving my own story. Isolated. Confused. Overwhelmed. Over and over, in study after study.

When I began volunteering as a menopause peer group facilitator and co-facilitator around the northern suburbs of Brisbane, I heard the same story again and again, just in different voices. So many women carrying some version of what I'd felt in that shower. Something had to change, and now.

My brain doesn't let a pattern go once it's noticed one, and it's never had much patience for injustice. As a late-diagnosed autistic ADHDer, both of those turned out to be exactly what this problem needed. I combined research, the stories I'd heard, and my own lived experience. And Menopause Understood was born.

I want you to feel informed instead of confused. Connected instead of isolated. Supported instead of alone. And eventually, at ease in your own menopause journey. Through short courses that explain what's really happening in your body, and a real community of women who get it, you don't have to figure this out by yourself.

I'm not a doctor, and I won't pretend to be one. What I bring is research, lived experience, warmth, and a genuine commitment to making this stage of life feel less overwhelming and a lot less lonely.
Welcome. I'm so glad you're here.

Our first course is the beginning of a full library, with each course covering its own topic. Here's where the catalogue is heading.
Why Doesn't My Body Feel Like Mine?
Understanding Hot Flushes, Vaginal/Urinary Changes, and Other Symptoms
An overview of the physical changes menopause can bring, from hot flushes to vaginal and urinary changes, so you know what to expect and why it happens.
It's Not Just in Your Head
Understanding Your Mood, Memory and Joint Symptoms
An overview of the mood, memory and joint changes that come with menopause, so you know they're real and not something you're imagining.
Understanding the Long-Term Health Changes That Come With Menopause
An overview of the long-term menopause-related changes to your bones, heart and brain health, so you know why they happen and why understanding them now matters.
Without Warning, the Mask Was Gone
An overview of how menopause and being neurodivergent can affect each other, so you know why that connection is worth paying attention to.
Nutrition, Sleep and Exercise During Menopause
An overview of exercise, sleep and nutrition during menopause, so you know why each one matters more than you might think.
Understanding Stress, Capacity and Self-Care in Menopause
An overview of what's really going on with your stress and capacity during menopause, so you know that making space for yourself isn't optional, it's necessary.
This Wasn't Supposed to Happen Yet
Understanding Early, Induced and Premature Menopause
An overview of early, induced and premature menopause, so you know your experience is just as valid even if it didn't follow the expected timeline.
Communicating with Your Doctor, Family and Friends About Menopause
An overview of how to start the conversation, whether it's with your doctor, your partner or your friends, so you know you don't have to carry this by yourself.

Most of us were never taught about menopause, so when symptoms start, it's easy to think there's something wrong with you.

Maybe you've fallen down a million rabbit holes of reels and podcasts and left feeling more confused than when you started. Maybe you've tried to explain it to your doctor, your partner, or your friends, and felt dismissed. It's okay that this is hard, and it's okay that you're looking for answers.
That's why I created What's Happening to Me? Understanding Every Stage of Your Menopause Journey.
It's a short course that walks you through the whole journey in order, from your first cycle changes to life after menopause, so you can stop piecing it together from scattered information online.

I'm Melissa. I'm currently completing a Master of Medical Science, where I'm researching women's interactions with menopause health information and services. But before any of that, I was a woman diagnosed with early menopause at 41, with more symptoms than I could count and no idea what was happening to me.
That experience, plus my research and the women I've met as a menopause peer group facilitator, is what this course is built on. It's the course I wish I'd had.
You don't have to keep working this out on your own. In one short course, you can know which stage you're likely in, what tends to come next, and have a free resource to keep coming back to.

How is this different from free information online?

Free information is everywhere, but it's scattered and often contradictory. This course brings it together in one clear, guided walkthrough, in order, grounded in published research and written with warmth, so you're not left piecing it together yourself.
What if I'm not sure this course is right for me?

If you're trying to work out which stage you might be in, this course is for you. Whether your cycle has only just started changing, you're in the thick of symptoms, or you're well past your last period, it'll help you place where you're likely to be and what tends to come next. It's also a good fit if you want to feel prepared for what's ahead, or to better support someone you love through it.
